# Understanding MICS6 data {#ch-whats-in-data}

This chapter is about what sits in a MICS6 download: which file is which, who appears in `fs`, and how the Foundational Learning Skills (FLS) assessment is scored.

MICS is a household survey with several questionnaires, so the microdata are several files with different units of observation. Using the wrong file, merging on an incomplete key, or treating a reading skip as ordinary missing data changes the population you describe.

``` text
HOUSEHOLD (hh)
   │
   ├── household members (hl)
   │
   └── one randomly selected child aged 5–17 (fs)
           │
           └── ages 7–14 may take the FLS assessment
```

For foundational learning, start with `fs`. Add household facts from `hh` and roster facts from `hl` when the question needs them.

The [MICS6 Manual for Statistical Data Analysis](https://data.unicef.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/MICS6-manual-for-stats-data-analysis-English_2020_v2.pdf) and UNICEF's [Foundational Learning Skills Module](https://data.unicef.org/resources/the-foundational-learning-skills-module/) are the official references.
